newsitem.title: UK: Enterprise Oil falls on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Enterprise Oil falls on profit-taking.

text.p: Shares in Enterprise Oil Plc fell sharply as profit-taking set in after the stocks breached the seven pound barrier last week to hit a record high of 701 pence.
Enterprise was down 12-1/2 pence by 0836 GMT, when 850,637 shares had changed hands.
Lower crude prices prompted investors to sell, dealers said. They also cited that as a reason for British Petroleum Co Plc losing 7-1/2 pence to 744.
Elsewhere in the oil exploration and production sector, SOCO International Plc rose 20-1/2 pence to 256, after the company announced its fourth Mongolian oil discovery.
SOCO was floated at the end of last month, after a share placing at 260 pence a piece. Turnnover in the shares was 661,379.
Cairn Energy Plc firmed two pence to 518, after broker SocGen repeated its "buy" recommendation because of the bright outlook of Cairn's operations in Bangladesh, SocGen analyst John Toalster said.
